newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-HAGI SEEKS FREEDOM FOR FOOTBALLERS TO MOVE OUTSIDE EU.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HAGI SEEKS FREEDOM FOR FOOTBALLERS TO MOVE OUTSIDE EU.

text.p: The agent for Gheorghe Hagi urged freedom of movement for all footballers on Tuesday but, but officials doubted the Romanian midfielder would succeed in a court case to extend the Bosman ruling beyond the EU.
"Soccer players are workers who should enjoy the freedom of movement," Ioan Becali told Reuters by phone from Spain.

The case of Belgian player Jean-Marc Bosman led to a rewriting of the rule-book concerning players' rights last year when a Brussels court banned quotas that limited the number of EU players in sports sides within the Union. It also changed the laws on players' transfers.

Bosman's lawyer, Jean-Louis Dupont, said last week he would take Hagi's case against FIFA, UEFA and Barcelona to court to plead for players from countries with special treaties with the Union to be treated on a par with EU players.
After the World Cup finals in Italy in 1990 Hagi moved successively to Spain's Real Madrid, Italy's Brescia and then Spanish side Barcelona.
Barcelona had asked Turkish club Galatasaray $1.8 million dollars for Hagi's transfer fee last summer, and have retained part of his final pay-cheque after both the club and Hagi refused to pay.
"Hagi's case includes all extra-community players, so it is important for European soccer as a whole," Becali said.
Up to 120 players from ex-communist east European countries play for EU sides, especially in Spain, Italy and Germany.
Romania's Soccer Federation (FRF) has voiced doubts over the chances Hagi's court case against FIFA, UEFA and Barcelona.
"I don't think that Hagi can get what he wants as long as his contract with Barcelona does not have a clause that he is free without paying transfer fees," said RSF spokesman Cristian Bivolaru.
The Bosman ruling acts only within the EU and is not binding for East European players who quit a Union side.
UEFA oficials said Hagi's claim had no legal grounds under accords between the European Union and the Balkan country, state news agency Rompres said.

"The EU and Romania only have a trade association accord which makes no reference to individuals," the agency quoted Jose Luis Villaseca, UEFA Control and Discipline Board president, as saying. REUTER
